speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of pain during urination; you also mentioned a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own. To better understand what is happening, have you noticed any redness or warmth over the affected knee, and do you have a history of gout or inflammatory bowel disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome), likely triggered by a sexually transmitted infection such as Chlamydia trachomatis, given the triad of asymmetric oligoarthritis, urethritis (pain with urination), and recent sexual activity with inconsistent condom use.
